statement: A classifier keyed on a tool's exact error wording breaks silently when the tool's next release rewords the message. git 2.56 changed the message for a .git file pointing at a missing gitdir from 'not a git repository: <gitdir>' to 'gitfile does not point to a valid repository: <.git file>'; Cejel recognised only the first, so on the new CI runner image a no-repository case classified as a failed git invocation and the scan threw, with no code change on either side. The end-to-end tests that caught it pass or fail with whatever git the host has, so they could not show which wording mattered. Rules: verify each recognised message against the tool's source at a named version and record the version beside the pattern; pin every known wording as a literal input to the classifier, so its tests do not depend on the installed tool; keep each new pattern anchored at the message start, with a fixed prefix, so a path inside the message still cannot choose the class.
